content.title: Golden State Warriors vs Denver Nuggets injury report: Who's playing, injured and questionable players, head-to-head records, team stats, and more (March 29, 2026)
content.text: Nikola Jokic of Nuggets vs Warriors (Image via AP Photo)The Golden State Warriors travel to Ball Arena on Sunday, March 29, 2026, to face the Denver Nuggets. This game comes at an important time in the season. Denver is trying to stay strong in the standings, while Golden State is fighting to keep its season alive.The two teams are coming in with very different situations. Denver is healthy and playing well. Golden State is dealing with many injuries and has a shorter rotation. That puts more pressure on younger players to step up.Golden State Warriors vs Denver Nuggets Injury report (March 29, 2026)Denver Nuggets • Nikola Jokić - Active • Jamal Murray - Active • Aaron Gordon - Active • Bruce Brown Jr. - Active • Cameron Johnson - Active • Christian Braun - Active • Tim Hardaway Jr. - Active • Hunter Tyson, Peyton Watson, DaRon Holmes II, Jonas Valančiūnas, Julian Strawther, Jalen Pickett, Curtis Jones, Spencer Jones - All activeDenver has no players on the injury list and will play at full strength.Israel Iran WarUS-Israel-Iran War News Live Updates: Middle East war day 30: Iran threatens to hit US universities; Gui Santos and Melton have also helped.Golden State Warriors vs Denver Nuggets Matchup breakdown (March 29, 2026)Curry’s absence vs Jokić’s controlWithout Stephen Curry, Golden State Warriors lose its main scorer and creator. The team will depend on Podziemski and Melton. Denver will run its offense through Jokić, who controls the game well.Perimeter shooting vs interior dominanceGolden State depends on three-point shooting and makes a lot of them. Denver plays stronger inside with size and rebounding, led by Jokić.Defensive balance and schedule pressureDenver’s defense is average. Golden State’s offense has not been consistent. The Warriors are also in a tough stretch of games, which makes this harder.This game shows two teams in different spots. Denver looks strong and healthy. Golden State is dealing with injuries but still trying to compete.
